chapter: Baton Rouge big band and New York
title: The Standard Oil big band and its photographs
summary: He was hired because of his clarinet and read only when he wanted; the interviewer counts instruments in two big-band photos.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Oh yes it was a big band. Well I read when I wanted to have a different one I did. In other words I was my own boss. I just told you I want to go to old man Weller. Weller? Weller? Weller here every time he come back he likes old man bringing his kid toys and say he'd bring me more dirt and poofy. Anything in the line of a musical instrument otherwise he got it. And man when that jazz band went out there you better not tell him that's gold.
It's not like that. You had a jazz band in this band?
Yeah the jazz band was taken out of there out of the big band.
In fact you got about eight trumpets or cornets here I can't tell which is which. Some of them are trumpets and some of them are carnets. We got a drum major here.
At least three saxophones. Three saxophones. Four because one of the little fellas not on that.

We really had a quartet in saxes. Four clarinets and a bass drum player, a cymbal player and a kettle drum player. Looks like a piccolo player in there. And about three peck horns. Maybe four. Maybe four peck horns and three trombone players, a baritone horn player and a sousaphone player. Yeah. And one man I can't see what he plays. Which one? That man next to the sousaphone player. Right there.

That's an old picture. It's a big band though. That again is a big band. That's a lead. Now I can't remember his waist pain. That's the French one. He's carrying under his arm. Hmm? He's got a French one under his arm. I can't see. It looks like one of these benders. He's got a little machine. He's got a little machine. He's got a little machine.
You don't remember what he played, huh? No, I can't recall. That's my fault. Let's see. Well, we got another picture.
Mm-hmm. All right. Let's see. In this picture you've got... What is this?

It's a little lighter. You've got like six trumpets of cornets, two baritone horns, four pec horns, a tuba, snad drum, bass drum. Then another, another sousaphone. That's it. Sousaphone and a tuba bow. Four trombones. Like two alphans. Let me see.

One's an alphan and one's a C melody, I think. C melody side. The other picture you have an alphan and a baritone and either a C melody or a tenon. It looks more like a tenon. Boy, you had some clarinets in there. You had five clarinets and a piccolo play. Well, that man holding that, that man must be the director.

You know that's just who he is. Yeah, he's a director. I see. It's just when you said director, it came right to him. Yeah. That's what he was. That's a director. I can't recall his name offhand, but that's what he was.
